insights.summary: Gilead delivered Q1 2026 revenue of $6.96 billion (+4% YoY) and net income of $2.02 billion (+54% YoY), driven by strong HIV portfolio growth (Biktarvy +7%, Descovy +38%) and Trodelvy momentum (+37%), partially offset by Veklury decline (-52% due to lower COVID hospitalizations) and cell therapy headwinds. However, management guidance is cautious as the company expects ~$11.5 billion in IPR&D charges in Q2 2026 from major acquisitions (Arcellx, Tubulis, Ouro), resulting in anticipated net loss for Q2 and full year 2026. The company maintains strong pricing power and operating cash flow generation ($2.54B in Q1), but faces ongoing litigation risks and competitive pressures in cell therapy.
keyQuotes: As a result of the recent acquisitions completed or announced above, we expect to record related charges of approximately $11.5 billion to Acquired in-process research and development expenses in the second quarter of 2026, which we expect to result in a net loss for the second quarter and full year 2026.

HIV product sales increased 10% to $5.0 billion for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to higher demand and average realized price, partially offset by unfavorable inventory dynamics.

Cell Therapy product sales decreased 12% to $407 million for the three months ended March 31, 2026, compared to the same period in 2025, primarily due to lower demand reflecting ongoing competitive headwinds.

insights.summary: Gilead reported 2% revenue growth to $29.4B and significant net income improvement to $8.5B in 2025, driven by strong HIV product sales growth (6%) and Liver Disease expansion, partially offset by Veklury decline (49% decrease due to lower COVID-19 hospitalizations). The company faces substantial regulatory headwinds including Medicare price negotiation, MFN pricing mandates, and tariff threats, though management has secured a 3-year tariff pause agreement. Management maintains neutral outlook with expected continued product sales growth offset by policy impacts and competitive pressures in Cell Therapy.
keyQuotes: During 2025, we delivered growth in our HIV product sales, introduced Yeztugo, the first and only twice-yearly HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis option available in the U.S., and expanded Livdelzi's market share in the treatment of primary biliary cholangitis.

In December 2025, Gilead reached an agreement with the administration to (1) pause the imposition of Section 232 tariffs on Gilead for three years, (2) implement MFN prices in Medicaid for select existing and future launched products, (3) set a new direct-to-patient price for Epclusa and (4) return a portion of increased international revenues to the U.S.
